pages.text: Water flows into salty water through a membrane, pulled by the osmotic pressure π = iMRT (van 't Hoff): two ions for each NaCl, M moles a litre, at 298 K. Push the salty side harder than π and the flow reverses: fresh water comes through. The flux grows with how far past π it is pushed.
$(thing)Set$(): Feed pressure.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Fouling: the membrane passes ±1%·d of its rated flow.
$(thing)Limits$(): Over the membrane's rated pressure.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Fresh water follows the flux.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Osmotic pressure: π = iMRT$(br)Water flux: J = A·(P − π)
